parsed.explanation: Thin trans-specific data, so extrapolation governs. Structural signals: no legal gender recognition, so a visitor is assessed against birth-sex documents; entrenched societal discrimination and taboo framing ('imported, contrary to local values'); no anti-discrimination law; no community infrastructure. Most serious: a public-morals offence with heavier-than-standard penalties, plus a local organisation documenting arrests on false accusations and torture/mistreatment of LGBTQ people by police — state-tolerated targeting with total impunity (2012 report shows extrajudicial violence by security forces). A trans person whose presentation draws scrutiny, or who is detained, faces that enforcement environment with no recourse; custody treatment is undocumented but the surrounding impunity is adverse. No presentation offence, no facility rule, and penalties are moderate, keeping this above the severe band; but documented police abuse, criminalised public affection, concealment-forced society and absent protections put it solidly in the high-risk band, near 0.25-0.35 profiles rather than reduced risk.
